data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Ensemble learning typically aggregates votes to make a single positive decision, whereas DeepReason's argumentative criticism seeks to actively retire or falsify specific positions.","Peer review generally operates on a fixed schedule of submission and review, while DeepReason's batched criticism is an ongoing dynamic process aiming for grounded extensions."],"overturn_conditions":["If the criticism process strictly requires deterministic Dung-style grounded extensions (unique and skeptical) rather than probabilistic sampling, the ensemble analogy does not apply."],"shared_structure":["Both DeepReason's school system and ensemble learning employ multiple independent agents evaluating a shared space of candidate models.","Both systems face a scaling limit where exhaustively evaluating all combinations or attacks becomes computationally intractable as the space grows."],"source_memory_refs":["https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ensemble_learning","https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review"],"transfer_claims":["Transferring the concept of subspace sampling from ensemble learning to DeepReason criticism can prioritize which rival positions to attack, circumventing the coverage debt by probabilistically focusing on the weakest warrants."]},"claim":"The criticism mechanism's near-zero retirement rate is caused by a superlinear explosion in coverage debt as rival positions grow from 18 to 60; replacing exhaustive per-target batched criticism with a Popperian-inspired, ensemble-sampled criticism model will optimize retirement without exhausting coverage budgets.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the Python simulation shows that exhaustive batched criticism maintains a linear retirement rate despite the growth from 18 to 60 rival positions, the coverage debt explosion hypothesis is falsified.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If evidence shows that DeepReason's existing closure rules already dynamically limit the effective attack space keeping coverage debt linear, the proposed ensemble sampling is redundant.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If Wikipedia's article on Popperian critical rationalism dictates that exhaustive coverage is mandatory to prevent false acceptances, the shift to probabilistic ensemble sampling is epistemologically invalid.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Under fixed criticism budgets, the number of required warrant comparisons scales poorly (superlinearly) with the number of accepted rival positions. By sandboxing a Python simulation of batched criticism where the rival space expands from 18 to 60, we can demonstrate the collapse in retirements. We can then introduce an ensemble sampling approach where a subset of critics probabilistically targets the weakest rivals (aligned with critical rationalism), forcing selective retirements rather than attempting full coverage. The simulation will contrast exhaustive coverage versus ensemble-sampled criticism to show which maintains a steady retirement rate.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
